The company's outperformance can be attributed to its strong customer relationships, strategic partnerships and comprehensive portfolio of power management, thermal management, liquid cooling and modular infrastructure solutions. VRT continues to benefit from accelerating AI-driven data center investments, increasing infrastructure density and growing demand for integrated power and cooling solutions. Expanding manufacturing capacity, improving operational efficiency and disciplined backlog execution further supported its strong performance. These factors are helping Vertiv to fend off its competitors from companies like Super Micro Computers and Amphenol.

Vertiv Capitalizes on Strong AI Data Center Growth

Vertiv is benefiting from accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, increasing demand for high-density data centers and growing adoption of advanced power and thermal management solutions. The company's comprehensive portfolio spanning liquid cooling, power distribution, UPS systems, switchgear and modular infrastructure positions it well to capitalize on rising power and cooling requirements across hyperscale and AI data centers.

Strong demand from hyperscalers, enterprises, and neocloud providers is driving Vertiv's growth. In the third quarter of 2026, revenues surged 61% year over year to $4.31 billion, supported by approximately 55% organic growth. Organic orders grew more than 100% year over year, reflecting robust customer demand and strengthening market positioning. Revenues increased 75% in the Americas, 50% in Asia-Pacific and 23% in EMEA.

Vertiv is also benefiting from expanding liquid cooling adoption as increasing rack densities require sophisticated thermal management solutions. Its converged infrastructure approach, combining power, cooling and modular deployment capabilities, is helping customers accelerate data center construction. Collaborations with NVIDIA NVDA, Dassault Systemes and Polar Data Centers are focused on reducing design and deployment timelines, potentially improving customers' returns on AI infrastructure investments.

The company is expanding manufacturing capacity across the Americas, EMEA and Asia-Pacific to address its growing backlog. Its strategic acquisitions of Utility Innovation Group and King Environmental Services further strengthen its power infrastructure and services capabilities. The transition toward 800-volt DC power architectures also presents an additional long-term growth opportunity.

Key Stats for Super Micro Stock

Current Price: $32.95

Target Price (Mid): ~$61

Street Target: ~$43

Potential Total Return: ~84%

Annualized IRR: ~14% / year

What Happened?

Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) said on October 20 that preliminary September-quarter revenue should land at $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion, against guidance of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. Shares closed at $35.81 on October 28, then fell 3.85% on October 29, with no catalyst reported, and 4.30% on October 30, when Intel's PC warning hit hardware stocks and Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) dropped 10.77%.

The October 30 close of $32.95 was 48 cents above the pre-update close. With preliminary numbers out, the November 3 report, due after the close, has to answer two questions the preview did not: how durable the neocloud business is, and whether the margin holds.

Staiger Says the Neocloud Worry Will Still Be There at $68 Billion

At Goldman Sachs' September 10 tech conference, analyst Katherine Murphy cited third-party data estimating a 40% market share for Super Micro in neocloud servers. She asked whether maturing neoclouds would turn to Taiwanese contract manufacturers or a lower-cost model. Michael Staiger, SVP of Corporate Development, said the concern "was around at $7 billion at $15 billion at $22 billion, at $39 billion, and it's going to exist at $68 billion," close to the midpoint of the $65 billion to $72 billion fiscal 2027 guide.

His defense was speed: integrated racks get customers online faster. Earlier in the session, explaining margins, he said "our systems at the neoclouds are serving hyperscalers."

The newer question is funding. On October 27, Reuters reported that Super Micro-backed Argentum AI is in talks for a $5 billion private credit deal to buy AI chips, citing two people familiar with the matter. Super Micro shares rose 7.34% that day. The same report said financing for neoclouds has tightened, so the talks point to both appetite for capacity and a harder path to funding it.

Super Micro Stock Price (TIKR)
Analysts Model a Thinner Margin Than September's

Staiger said the September quarter's 10.6% gross margin guide midpoint included pressure from contracts that "potentially dug through from the prior quarter," and that more integrated rack components carry a higher margin. The preliminary 12.0% to 12.5% beat it. As of November 2, analysts tracked by TIKR expect fiscal 2027 gross margin of around 10.3%.

Revenue estimates lag too: TIKR's September-quarter consensus of around $16.3 billion sits below the preliminary low end.
